analysis.title: nVENT Electric Plc. (NVT): 3Q beat and raise, record orders, raising estimates
key_insights: NVT reported 3Q26 segment EBITA of $371mn, +7% vs FactSet consensus of $345mn, with Systems Protection +6% and Electrical Connections +10% vs consensus. Adj. EPS was $1.52 (+67% YoY) vs GS $1.44 and FactSet consensus $1.40.
Organic growth was +43.9% (GS +41.8%). Systems Protection grew +53.7% (GS +55.0%) and Electrical Connections +23.2% (GS +14.0%), with double-digit growth across all verticals and geographies.

Electrical Connections accelerated for a second consecutive quarter. Management raised FY26 outlook for Industrial and Comm/Resi to high-single-digit organic growth (prior mid-single-digit), which GS reads as short-cycle markets inflecting positively.

Segment adj. operating margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 24.5% despite ~$60mn of inflation in 3Q (including ~$20mn of tariffs), as price nearly covered inflation. FY26 tariff headwind is now ~$105mn vs ~$100mn prior.
Systems Protection margin expanded ~260 bps YoY to 23.1%. Electrical Connections margin contracted ~180 bps YoY due to inflation and growth investments.

3Q orders were a record, up ~low-double-digit % on top of ~65% growth a year ago. Backlog grew to ~$2.6bn from ~$2.5bn in 2Q26. Management said October orders are strong and backlog should keep building as the mix shifts to longer-cycle work, particularly with Maverick.

NVT announced a new 400k sq. ft. engineered building solutions facility in Arizona serving data centers and power utilities, with production slated for mid-2027 alongside Blaine 2. Blaine 1 is ramping ahead of plan. FY26 capex is now ~$140mn, +~50% YoY.

The Maverick Power acquisition closed October 1 for $1.75bn (~11.5x 2026E adj. EBITDA, ~10.5x including tax benefits), with up to $550mn of additional consideration tied to 2027-28 performance. It was funded with $800mn of 10-year senior notes, ~$850mn of additional debt at close and cash on hand. Leverage is expected within the 2.0-2.5x target by year-end.

Maverick brings ~$700mn of 2026E revenue, ~1.5mn sq. ft. of manufacturing footprint and a strong backlog, and will be reported in Electrical Connections. It roughly doubles NVT's data center content opportunity to ~$2mn/MW and adds LV/MV switchgear and an 800 VDC power rack, positioning NVT as a system-level power plus liquid cooling provider.

4Q is an investment quarter for Maverick (mid-teens margins), pulling total 4Q incrementals to the low-20s vs mid-20s for the core. GS estimates Maverick adds $0.40 to 2027 EPS (~6% of FY27E), assuming ~25% revenue growth to ~$875mn, ~17% adj. operating margin, ~$65mn annualized incremental net interest and a ~22% tax rate.

NVT raised its FY26 EPS guide to $5.36-$5.39 (from $5.00-$5.10) and organic sales growth to +38-39% (from +32-34%). GS sees conservatism because the guide implies roughly flat total revenue sequentially despite ~$200mn of Maverick sales. Management cited normal seasonality and prudence as suppliers scale capacity. 4Q EPS guide is $1.30-$1.33 and FCF conversion is ~90-95% (unchanged).

GS raises FY26/FY27/FY28 EPS to $5.40/$7.25/$8.75 (from $5.25/$6.75/$8.00) and keeps a Buy rating. The 12-month PT falls to $188 from $192 on a Q5-Q8 EBITDA multiple of 16.0x (vs 19.0x prior), reflecting a de-rating across the peer group.
The stock is down 13.0% over 3 months and 11.8% over 6 months in absolute terms, and up 20.7% over 12 months. Price is $125.98, implying 49.2% upside to the PT.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q beat and raise with record orders and Maverick adding data center content. PT trimmed from $192 to $188 on a lower 16.0x target multiple reflecting a peer-group de-rating.

sector_views.rationale: Short-cycle industrial and comm/resi markets are inflecting positively, and data center and power utility demand is driving record orders.
